## Why
rebar's mutating verbs follow the classic Unix rule of silence: `link`, `unlink`, `comment`, `tag`, `edit`, `set-file-impact` exit 0 with empty stdout on success (only `create`/`revert`/`claim` print, because they return generated state). Observed operational cost (2026-08-14, bug clubby-circular-halicore): success and silent idempotent no-op are indistinguishable on stdout (failure is already distinguishable — nonzero exit + stderr — but agents don't trust silence), so agents routinely run a second `rebar show` to verify their own write — an extra store read per mutation — and one agent misread a silent success as a failed write, filed a spurious bug, and retried the identical command (which no-opped silently, compounding the misdiagnosis). Modern CLI practice (clig.dev; kubectl/git/gh/terraform) prints a one-line confirmation of every state change precisely because the caller cannot otherwise see what mutated. rebar's primary operators are agents that must confirm their writes; the confirmation belongs in the mutation's own output.

## Plan
1. **Outcome signal at the write seam.** Core write functions that today return `None` (e.g. `add_dependency`, comment/tag/edit writers) gain a small structured return (e.g. `WriteOutcome(wrote: bool, detail: str)` or equivalent minimal tuple) so the CLI layer can distinguish wrote-vs-noop WITHOUT a follow-up store read. Returning a value where `None` was returned is backward-compatible for existing callers (none consume the return; verified by reference sweep before change). No new store reads; no event-schema change.
2. **One-line stdout confirmation per mutating verb**, kubectl-style, built only from arguments + the outcome signal: `linked <src-alias> -> <target-alias> (<relation>)`, `unlinked ...`, `comment added to <alias>`, `tagged <alias>: +a +b`, `edited <alias>: description`, `impact set on <alias>: <n> paths`. No counts or derived state that would require reducing the ticket.
3. **Idempotent no-ops SAY SO**, exit 0 unchanged: `already linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`. The idempotent contract is preserved — the notice is output-only, driven by the outcome signal; no event written (store-event count asserted in tests).
4. **Channel discipline decided now:** confirmations print ONLY in the default text output mode. Under the existing structured output flag (`--output json` / `-o json`, the parse_output convention), stdout stays exclusively the JSON document — mutating verbs that support `--output json` include the outcome as a structured field (e.g. `"outcome": "linked"|"noop"`) instead of a text line. A new global `--quiet`/`-q` flag suppresses the text confirmation for scripts; errors/exit codes unaffected. (A config-key equivalent is OUT OF SCOPE.)
5. **Confirmation goes to STDOUT** (it is the command's result, not a diagnostic); warnings/logs stay on stderr. Exit codes remain the programmatic contract, unchanged.
6. **Inventory from the dispatch tables, not a hand list:** enumerate mutating verbs from `_commands/__init__.py`'s actual dispatch/write sets (`_WRITES_FULL` / `_DISPATCH_PRIMARY`), apply the pattern uniformly; verbs that already print (`create`, `revert`, `claim`, `transition`) keep their output normalized to the same style. MCP tools are OUT OF SCOPE (their outputSchemas already return structured results).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each mutating CLI verb (enumerated from the dispatch write-set, not hand-listed) prints a one-line stdout confirmation naming the operation and resulting state, built solely from arguments + the write seam's outcome signal; per-verb tests assert the line and that no additional store read/reduce is performed to build it.
- [ ] Core write seams return an outcome signal distinguishing wrote-vs-noop; a reference sweep confirms no existing caller consumed the prior `None` return (behavior-preserving).
- [ ] Idempotent no-op paths (at minimum: re-link of an identical active edge) print an explicit already-X notice, still exit 0, still write no event (store-event count asserted).
- [ ] `--quiet` suppresses text confirmations; under `--output json` stdout remains a single valid JSON document with the outcome as a structured field (tested).
- [ ] Confirmations on stdout, logs/warnings on stderr (tested via captured streams); no exit-code changes (existing exit-code contract tests stay green).
- [ ] docs/user-guide.md + cli-reference regenerated; `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
